'hand' presence is benchmarked, but a rigorous omission judgment needs to confirm the expected hand REGION was visible (not merely cropped out of frame) -- evidence_rule_engine.py's existing evaluate_omission() primitive gates on 'region_visible', which needs spatial/bbox information. A lower-rigor presence-only proxy (person detected + hand absent) is possible but was not what that primitive was designed to certify.

'hand' is benchmarked, but 'exaggerated' is inherently a relative-SIZE judgment (this part vs. a reference, e.g. the whole figure) -- needs bounding boxes on both, not just presence.

Compound rule: colour (already measurable) + face (benchmarked) + isolation (a spatial relationship between detected figures -- needs bboxes, not yet built, Phase 2C.3 Stage D). Blocked at its weakest link.
observability_class=process_required -- a behavioral/process observation, not visible in a static image.
'Excessive' has no natural detector output -- needs a count/density attribute with a defensible threshold, not a presence detection.

'Background' is a region, not any of the 10 benchmarked object classes -- needs a region-level presence/extent judgment (segmentation-adjacent), plus a figure-vs-background spatial relationship on top (Phase 2C.3 Stage D) once the region exists.
